translations.answer: The author observed jitter in the real-time control loop after configuring real-time group limits and attempting to adjust process and child process priorities. A/B testing confirmed the jitter was caused by I2C IMU read, and the issue was resolved by isolating the I/O from the real-time path. The problem was not fixed by using a low-latency kernel alone. The effective fix was to isolate the I/O and observe stable behavior after removal or isolation. The credibility is limited as there is no formal cross-verification or independent replication available.
translations.applicability: Raspberry Pi 5, 250 Hz, low-latency kernel, and real-time path directly reads I2C IMU.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Configure real-time group limits; use chrt to adjust process and child process priorities; disable I2C IMU read; maintainers suggest printing time variables.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Remove or isolate I2C IMU read and observe control loop jitter resolution.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Do not use the same phenomenon to qualitatively determine the period parameter; print current_time, previous_time, and measured_period in the ros2_control node at the same location.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Remove/isolate the I2C IMU read to resolve the jitter observed by the author.
translations.details.environments.0: Raspberry Pi 5; controller_manager 250 Hz; low-latency kernel; real-time group limits configured afterward; not precise version of ROS 2/ros2_control used.
translations.details.limits.0: No mention of using asynchronous I/O, independent thread, or specific driver fix; only confirmed stability after disabling the I2C IMU read.
translations.details.limits.1: Cannot directly extrapolate low-latency kernel results to all hardware and RT kernels.
translations.details.outcomes.0: I2C-related jitter confirmed by the author via A/B testing; update period parameter issue not closed-loop.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How should I2C read and the update period parameter be diagnosed when the ros2_control 250 Hz control loop exhibits large jitter?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Avoid unbounded blocking I/O in real-time control threads; monitor worst-case execution time and deadline miss.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed the large jitter comes from the I2C IMU read; the period parameter issue remains undiagnosed.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Actual time difference fluctuates between ~1.1-6.9 ms; the update() period parameter does not match the author's offline time difference.
translations.source.title: ros2_control control loop jitter and update period anomaly must be separated and diagnosed
translations.terms.2: Real-time scheduling priority (实时调度优先级)
